Walkthrough · every screen

The single, current design: brand, panels, every state in light and dark, desktop and phone. Sample change: due dates for a small todo app. DESIGN.md and PRODUCT.md describe this page.

Brand Panels No tool panel The stepper shows where you are Main state Two kinds of walkthrough Files within a step File headers in one rhythm Per-file explanations Readable explanations Your own line comments Lines picked Session preparing steps Step list Folded step, with real reasons Markdown file Image file Checklist Decided step Changed step Being checked A finding that arrives late Note with replies Notes and their menu Flag asking for a note (typing); editing an [AI] draft before accepting Session status Summary step Help: what things mean Appearance Server unreachable List page Read-only export Main state at 390px 390px

Brand

Mark, wordmark, favicon and app icon; one ultramarine (configurable) for the few places colour carries meaning.

Panels

Tool windows, the JetBrains way: each panel has a title bar with a hide button; a hidden panel collapses to a labelled button on its edge (left: To review, Explanation; right: Checklist). Default: the queue open, the rest on their edges. Keys 1–3 toggle them. The tool panel is gone: its notes were already on their lines, and its session messages and notes on removed code now live on the Session messages page.

File headers in one rhythm Round 3

Five files, two opened and three collapsed (one Viewed). Every header sits flush on the rule under the one before it, opened or collapsed, so the list never jumps when a file opens. Flush is right: the 1px rule and the 36px header already separate files; any gap would have to be the same for every header and would only push the code down.

Five-paragraph explanation and a note with a list

Light

Parse due dates in the API

Undecided

This step teaches the API to accept a due date on create and update. Both handlers read an optional dueDate from the body and pass it through a new helper before saving.

parseDueDate returns a Date for a valid string and null when the value is missing. Today it also returns null for a string it cannot parse, which is the behaviour the findings below question.

What changes for callers

  • POST /tasks accepts dueDate as an ISO 8601 string.
  • PATCH /tasks/:id accepts it too, and currently clears the date when the field is absent.
  • Responses include dueDate as an ISO string or null.

The database column comes from step 2 and is nullable, so existing tasks keep working without a date. Nothing in the list view reads the field yet; that arrives in step 6.

Your review rules say invalid input should return 400 with the field name. The helper does not do that yet.

The migration from step 2 already ran on the sample data, so you can try the new field locally with npm run dev and a request like the one in the docs.

See the API rules and the open finding on line 29 before deciding.

src/api/tasks.ts+10 −2
26+function parseDueDate(value?: string): Date | null {
27+ if (!value) return null;
28+ const date = new Date(value);
29+ return isNaN(date.getTime()) ? null : date;
Findingline 29

A typo in the date becomes null and clears it, instead of a 400.

  • Return 400 with { field: "dueDate" }.
  • Reject impossible dates like 2026-02-30.
  • Keep a missing value as “no change” on PATCH.

30+}
